newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Peters says NZ tariff removal critical.
newsitem.headline: Peters says NZ tariff removal critical.

text.p: New Zealand treasurer Winston Peters told an Australian audience on Wednesday that tariff removal was critical if New Zealand was to become more competitive.
"Removing remaining tariffs, for example, is critical if New Zealand is to become more competitive in the things we do best," Peters told a Trans-Tasman businses circle luncheon in Sydney.

As part of the New Zealand coalition government's plan to create a competitive business environment, it would increase its efforts for an open skies aviation agreement with Australia and others, Peters said.
The government would also review vehicle tariffs by the end of 1997 to achieve a swift move to zero tariffs from the year 2000.
The government would also set a timetable next year for complete free trade ahead of the 2010 deadline set by the Asia Pacific Economic Co-operation Agreement (APEC).
Peters' plan for free trade contrasts with the Australian governments hesitation in recent months to speed up tariff reform.
The Australian government decided early last month to reject official advise that it cut car import tariffs to five percent by 2005.
The conservative Australian coalition instead decided to hold car tariffs at 10 percent until 2005.
